_schema.real_world: human-readable description of the actual incident
_schema.root_cause_keywords: tokens our pipeline output should match somewhere; used for token-overlap scoring
_schema.expected_constraint_themes: themes we'd hope to see in stakeholder constraints
_schema.expected_conflicts: stakeholder pairs we'd expect to see in conflict
_schema.would_have_caught_if: what specific output would constitute 'would have caught it'

01_atlassian_app_deletion.real_world: Atlassian April 2022: ~800 customer sites entirely deleted because Team A handed Team B site-level IDs instead of app-level IDs.
expected_constraint_themes: cross-team handoff approval gate
ID format / schema verification before bulk action
dry-run on a small sample before full execution
customer notification before destructive ops
rollback strategy or per-site backup
01_atlassian_app_deletion.would_have_caught_if: any constraint or conflict references identifier-format verification, sample/dry-run before bulk delete, or cross-team handoff approval

02_cloudflare_mcp_rollout.real_world: Cloudflare June 21, 2022: stepped rollout reached 19 spine locations; 'steps weren't small enough' so all 19 went down together.
expected_constraint_themes: single-location canary before any batch
per-batch traffic-loss monitor gate
automated rollback on traffic anomaly
long enough soak window between batches
smaller batch size than 'all 19'
02_cloudflare_mcp_rollout.would_have_caught_if: any constraint or conflict references single-location canary, post-deploy traffic gate, or batch-size limits

03_cloudflare_dc_failover.real_world: Cloudflare Nov 2-4, 2023: 41-hour control-plane outage because many services believed to be HA were single-region in PDX-01; no recent failover drill.
expected_constraint_themes: verify each service's actual HA configuration before failing over
regular failover drills on a fixed cadence
service-dependency audit before failover
explicit per-service HA approval gate
fall-back order if a 'HA' service turns out to be single-region
03_cloudflare_dc_failover.would_have_caught_if: any constraint or conflict references HA verification, failover drills, or undocumented dependencies on a single region

04_gitlab_db_replica.real_world: GitLab Jan 31, 2017: engineer ran rm -rf on db1 (primary) instead of db2 (replica); 5 of 6 backup procedures had silently failed.
expected_constraint_themes: verify the target host before any destructive op
verify backups are working RIGHT NOW before destructive op
two-person concurrent verification of host identity
no rm without a typed-out confirmation
fatigue / time-of-day awareness
04_gitlab_db_replica.would_have_caught_if: any constraint or conflict references host/target verification before destructive op, backup-validity check immediately before, or two-person concurrent confirmation

05_linear_cascade_migration.real_world: Linear Jan 24, 2024: generated migration with ON DELETE CASCADE deleted production data; PR reviewed by multiple engineers, local test ran against smaller snapshot that did not reproduce.
expected_constraint_themes: review the generated DDL itself, not just the migration intent
dry-run against a production-shape replica
explicit cascade-detection step in PR review
soak / quiet period before column drops
two-stage drop: deprecate first, drop later
05_linear_cascade_migration.would_have_caught_if: any constraint or conflict references cascade-aware DDL review, dry-run on a production-equivalent dataset, or two-stage column deprecation
